I read this once probably about 10 years ago. I remember being disappointed in the book for a few reasons. Mainly because it offered so few answers to a great mystery.

However, I now realize that was the point. Some mysteries simply don't have an answer. You're left wondering and speculating, but will never be able to draw an absolute conclusion.

I think this was the intended purpose. An intentional feeling of dissatisfaction towards the loose ends that remain unexplained.

Good book, not great, but good. It has some great imagery in it. King does a great job of describing how inexplicable and indescribable the foreign creatures were. How unsettling they are to the human psyche due to just how foreign they appear. The absolute wrongness of something that we can't even begin to understand.

Towards the end when Sandy glimpsed into that other wordly place, gave me goose bumps. I think I may take a crack at trying to draw the scene he described.

Anyways 6/10 would recommend, but not highly.
